text: The fix works correctly. The issue was a single-character off-by-one bug in `wrapper/wrap.py`: the greedy packing condition used `len(current) + 1 + len(word) < width`, which rejected words that would make the line *exactly* `width` characters long. Changing it to `<= width` matches the documented behavior ("a line may be exactly `width` long"), so `wrap("aaa bbb", 7)` now returns `["aaa bbb"]` and paragraphs fill each line to the requested width. Overlong-word splitting is unaffected, and all tests pass.
